newsitem.title: CHINA: Yankee market favourable for Asian issuers - Merril.
newsitem.headline: Yankee market favourable for Asian issuers - Merril.

text.p: Tapping the U.S. bond market may be an attractive option for Asian borrowers, Spencer Lake, director of debt capital markets with Merrill Lynch, said on Tuesday.

He said the Yankee market offered high liquidity, a stable interest rate environment and a wider product range. Moreover, the U.S. Treasury yield curve is reasonably low by historical standards, Lake added.
Lake was speaking at a debt market conference in Hong Kong.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond was yielding 6.56 percent on Tuesday.
U.S. investors also tend to be more receptive to longer-dated paper than their European counterparts.
"They (US investors) are willing to take 30-year as opposed to 10-year positions and take the spread enhancement" said Lake.
He said rated Asian credits trade at an attractive premium over similarly rated U.S. and European issues, increasing their allure to U.S. investors.
Issuing longer-dated paper makes sense for Asian investors in terms of balance sheet management as the return on projects can be quickly identified, said Lake.
Lake said more Asian issuers were tapping the Yankee market.
Last week, three Asian issuers priced Yankee bonds worth a total of US$800 million and many more issues are in the pipeline.
